care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

## Your Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment

### Result: **INDETERMINATE** ❓

I've assessed your situation for Alex (11 years old), and while you meet most of the eligibility criteria, there's a critical piece of information that prevents me from giving you a definitive answer.

### What You Meet:
✅ Alex is under 16 years old  
✅ You live in the UK  
✅ You contribute £50/week towards Alex's upkeep (meeting the financial responsibility requirement)  
✅ No one else living with Alex is claiming Child Benefit  
✅ Alex is not working full-time, receiving benefits, or in a disqualifying apprenticeship  

### The Critical Issue:
⚠️ **Alex has been in hospital or residential accommodation for 15 weeks**

According to the rules:
- Child Benefit normally continues for up to **12 weeks** while a child is in hospital or residential accommodation
- After 12 weeks, you can **only continue** receiving Child Benefit if you are **regularly spending money on Alex** while they're in hospital (e.g., buying clothes, providing pocket money, purchasing personal items or treats)

### What You Need to Do:

Since it's unclear whether you're regularly spending money on Alex during their hospital stay, **you'll need to contact HMRC** to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Clarify what counts as "regularly spending money"
- Review your individual circumstances
- Make a definitive decision on your eligibility

📞 **Contact HMRC Child Benefit Office:**  
- Phone: 0300 200 3100
- More information: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

If you **are** regularly spending money on Alex while they're in hospital, you should remain eligible. If not, your Child Benefit may have stopped after the first 12 weeks of their hospital stay.

tool_response.help_text: Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation. CUMULATIVE RULE: If child returns within 28 days of leaving, time counts towards 12-week limit. Multiple stays within 28 days are added together.

criteria.calculation_method: Sum all hospital/residential stays. If gap between stays is less than 28 days, count both stays towards cumulative total. If gap is 28+ days, reset counter.
criteria.example: 10 weeks hospital + 15 day gap + 3 weeks hospital = 13 weeks cumulative (exceeds limit)
